key_insight: WorldGuide turns video generation into a closed-loop, goal-directed process: it does not just predict the next frame sequence, it decides the next action from the current generated state, executes it, and checks whether the task is finished. This makes long-horizon procedural task execution more adaptive and reliable than open-loop video generation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between plausible video synthesis and actual task completion in long-horizon procedural workflows. Existing open-loop models cannot react to their own outputs, while many closed-loop methods depend on pretrained executors or indirect verification rather than a unified goal-directed world model.
method: Build a video world model that conditions generation on the current generated state and task goal.
Use a closed-loop cycle of action selection, execution, and completion checking to adapt to outcomes.
Support procedural tasks where each next step depends on what the model has already generated.
Reduce reliance on external executors or weak proxy signals for verifying progress.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more practical framework for agentic video generation and procedural planning, especially when tasks require feedback-aware execution over long horizons. It can improve robustness in simulation, robotics-like settings, and interactive content generation.

paper_title: WorldGuide: Goal-Directed Video World Model for Procedural Task Execution
